title: Anticoncentration of the Permanent in Ginibre Ensembles
abstract: Let $\mathbb{K}\in\{\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C},\mathbb{H}\}$, put $β=\dim_{\mathbb{R}}\mathbb{K}$, and let $G_n^{\mathbb{K}}$ be an $n\times n$ matrix with i.i.d. standard $\mathbb{K}$-Gaussian entries, namely a standard $\mathbb{K}$-Ginibre matrix. We prove that the normalized row-ordered permanent $W_n^{\mathbb{K}}=\operatorname{per}_{\mathbb{K}}G_n^{\mathbb{K}}/\sqrt{n!}$ has a radial density $p_n^{\mathbb{K}}$ satisfying $\|p_n^{\mathbb{K}}\|_\infty=p_n^{\mathbb{K}}(0)\lesssim_βn^{(β+2)/4}$ and $\sup_{z\in\mathbb{K}}\mathbb{P}(|W_n^{\mathbb{K}}-z|\leq\varepsilon)\lesssim_βn^{(β+2)/4}\varepsilon^β$. In particular, for $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{C}$, this resolves the Permanent Anticoncentration Conjecture of Aaronson and Arkhipov. The proof compares the squared Gaussian permanent with the squared (Study) determinant in Laplace-transform order.
summary: This theoretical paper proves the 'Anticoncentration' property for the permanent of Ginibre random matrices over real, complex, and quaternionic fields. By comparing the permanent to the determinant using advanced tools like Laplace transforms, it resolves a major conjecture (PACC) and establishes tight bounds on the distribution of this key random matrix observable.
main_problem: The paper addresses the 'Anticoncentration of the Permanent' for Ginibre ensembles, a problem related to the permanent Anticoncentration Conjecture (PACC). It seeks to establish bounds on the distribution of the normalized row-ordered permanent.
main_result: For $K=\mathbb{C}$, the authors resolve the PACC by proving that the normalized permanent has a radial density with specific concentration bounds. They also established general anticoncentration results for $\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{C},$ and $\mathbb{H}$ fields.
method: The proof employs advanced techniques comparing the squared Gaussian permanent to the squared determinant in Laplace-transform order, utilizing inductive arguments and characteristic functions derived from properties of Gaussian distributions over different algebras ($\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{C}, \mathbb{H}$).

paper_structure: The paper develops results by first establishing benchmarks using the determinant and Study determinant across different fields. It then uses inductive arguments, characteristic functions, and specialized comparison theorems (like Lemma C.5) to prove the anticoncentration bounds for the permanent itself.
why_interesting: While highly mathematical, random matrix theory is foundational to quantum physics, especially in characterizing spectral statistics and entanglement measures derived from Gaussian ensembles. The study of permanents versus determinants touches upon non-Gaussian correlations relevant in complex physical models.
